page: Vultr voc-s-1c-8gb-150s-amd is a member of the Optimized Cloud Compute family, featuring a single dedicated AMD EPYC physical core on the x86_64 architecture. Operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, this server is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio. Local storage consists of a bundled 150 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The processor features a 32 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 vector extensions, SHA-NI cryptography, and AMD SVM virtualization.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-threaded performance due to the single-vCPU limitation. The server achieves top-tier single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, ranking in the top 10%, and demonstrates strong single-threaded compression and decompression capabilities. However, multi-core benchmarks, such as Geekbench and PassMark CPU tests, fall into the bottom 10% to 25% categories. Memory performance is moderate, with large-block read and write bandwidth averaging around 40.43 GB/sec and 36.8 GB/sec respectively, while small-block cached reads remain in the bottom 25%.

From a resource density perspective, this server offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:8, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound tasks that do not require high parallel processing power. Tradeoffs include poor multi-threaded scaling, low static web serving throughput, and weak database operation metrics. Consequently, this configuration is suited for lightweight single-threaded applications, basic text processing, small-scale memory-cached services, or low-concurrency development environments rather than heavy parallel computing or high-traffic web hosting.
